summary: The tampered-advice test never reaches the reply-vs-command-plan comparison it claims to prove.
failure_scenario: The test NULLs channel_messages.command_id and edits the envelope. A NULL command_id makes the reply 'legacy era', and _validated_stored_reply_fact only calls validated_channel_command_reply when reply_command_id is not None. The run fails on the era/provenance guard instead. A regression that drops the payload-vs-plan check while keeping command_id intact (the real forgery) is not caught here, and the test asserts no failure reason.
evidence: Temporarily replaced the validated_channel_command_reply(...) call in _sqlite_channels._validated_stored_reply_fact with 'pass'; test_a_tampered_advice_reply_never_becomes_a_successful_output still passed. Reverted. Pre-existing.

summary: No test covers the actor clause of validated_approval_reply (carried.actor.actor_id != reply.sender_actor_id).
failure_scenario: _force_impossible_approval_reply always uses the same actor (APPROVER) for the approval record and the reply, so the subject and run tests exercise only two of the three clauses behind 'decides a run, actor, or subject'. An approval whose carried actor differs from the authenticated reply sender (owner identity) would be accepted if that clause regressed.
evidence: Deleted the actor clause in core/human.py:validated_approval_reply; tests/e2e/test_standard_human_components.py, tests/api/test_request_bound_approval.py, tests/api/test_channel_mutations.py, tests/core, tests/substrate/channels (579 tests) all passed. A wider run (tests/api, journal, runtime, e2e) was started but stopped before finishing, so other suites were not checked. Reverted. Pre-existing.

summary: The 'endpoint-rw' drift case cannot reach the read-only flag check.
failure_scenario: mounts[4].replace('ro','rw') also rewrites 'provider' to 'prwvider' in the mount point /opt/native-startup/provider.sock. topology() then fails with 'endpoint must be one read-only leaf mount' because the leaf is missing, not because the flag is rw. A mutant that removes the 'ro' flag check on the leaf mount survives. pytest.raises(ValueError) is satisfied by any ValueError.
evidence: Removed ` or "ro" not in leaf[0][5].split(",")` from tests/substrate/_provider_bootstrap.py (temporarily); all 6 test_actual_namespace_preflight cases passed. Reverted.

summary: Any AssertionError counts as a kill, including one raised by production code reached through the mutant.
failure_scenario: pytest_runtest_makereport accepts AssertionError/pytest.fail from the call phase without checking that it came from a test assertion. A mutant that trips an internal `assert` in production code, or a helper that calls pytest.fail, is credited as KILLED although no test assertion compared an outcome. This contradicts the 'a mutant error is not a kill' rule.

summary: descendants() reads /proc/<pid>/task/<pid>/children, which lists only children forked by that one thread.
failure_scenario: A descendant forked from a non-main thread of the owner or supervisor is absent from the inventory. The later 'all(birth(pid) != started)' reaping assertions then cover only the processes that were seen, and len(observed) >= 4 is only a lower bound.

summary: logged_turn() picks the turn/start reply by 'id' equality alone, without requiring a result and no method.
failure_scenario: A server-initiated request logged before the real reply with the same numeric id is selected. reply['result'] then raises KeyError, so the lane fails loudly instead of folding the right reply; the id match is not proof of the reply.
The double accepts any capability id whenever the graph hash matches, so a test that passes the wrong capability to the admission question still sees the accepting path.
